title: Harden audit controls against stalled refreshes
summary: Bound Reports refreshes, separate audit busy state by operation, and keep authoritative command completion independent from best-effort page refreshes.
reason: A stalled or rejected follow-up refresh could leave unrelated audit controls disabled, misclassify a successful command as failed, or retain disabled dynamic row actions after authoritative source counts were already rendered.
behavior_before: Audit commands shared one global busy lock and awaited unbounded full-page refreshes, so one stalled read could disable unrelated controls indefinitely and a refresh rejection could overwrite a successful command result.
behavior_after: Source edit, source scan, start, stop, policy, and triage operations own separate locks. Command results release their lock before a bounded 15-second background refresh, and refresh failures append a warning while controls remain available.
tests_added: Maintenance/Reports browser smoke compresses the 15-second timeout and verifies a never-resolving refresh warns without relocking controls.
Maintenance/Reports browser smoke verifies Stop Audit is available after accepted start while audit progress refresh remains pending.
Maintenance/Reports browser smoke verifies a completed score-policy save reports Saved before its background refresh.
Maintenance/Reports browser smoke verifies a new audit immediately after an accepted stop is not hidden by the locally normalized stopped snapshot.
Maintenance/Reports browser smoke verifies a pending source scan locks only related controls.
Maintenance/Reports browser smoke verifies a rejected refresh preserves the successful command result.
Maintenance/Reports browser smoke verifies an active-run refresh warning survives the one-second running-state timer.
Maintenance/Reports browser smoke verifies pending audit lifecycle commands symmetrically lock source-registry commands.
Maintenance/Reports browser smoke verifies stale audit progress does not block selected sources.
